newsitem.title: BURUNDI: Hutu parliamentarian feared dead in Burundi.
newsitem.headline: Hutu parliamentarian feared dead in Burundi.

text.p: A Hutu member of parliament from Burundi's Frodebu party was missing, feared dead, on Tuesday after his burnt-out car was found in the south of the country.
Frodebu Secretary-General Augustin Nzojibwami told Reuters Paul Sinduhero and his driver had been missing since Saturday when their car was found in the southern province of Makamba.

"His car was found burned on the road to (the border town of) Mugina. The population of Makamba says he is dead. We hope it is not true," Nzojibwami said. He said he could not confirm Sinduhero had been killed because no bodies had been found.
Venerand Bakevyumusaya, a senior Frodebu member and former foreign minister, said 22 Frodebu parliamentarians had been assassinated since ethnic massacres and civil war began in 1993.
Sinduhero was driving to Tanzania where he was to pick up his family from the lake port of Kigoma where they had lived in exile since April 1996. His wife confirmed he never arrived.

The wife of the Frodebu speaker of the national assembly was wounded late in May when a landmine exploded under her car in the capital Bujumbura. The capital has been hit by a string of mine explosions this year.
More than 150,000 people have been killed in massacres and civil war between the Tutsi-dominated army and Hutu rebels since the assassination of Burundi's first Hutu president in October 1993.
